classification.difficultyReason: Construct a parallelogram using corresponding angles, justify parallel sides and verify side and diagonal properties by measurement.

content.prompt: Construct a parallelogram $ABCD$ as follows. Start with the interval $DC$.

spec.description: Horizontal opposite sides and right-sloping opposite sides; rightward baseline extension, three dashed red ray extensions and three corresponding 70-degree angles. Ordinary source-blue segments are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The rays from D and C make equal corresponding angles of 70 degrees with the baseline. The ray through A forms another corresponding 70-degree angle, giving AB parallel to DC.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied construction lines and angle labels remain visible; diagonals and their intersection are student responses.

answer.short: An accurately constructed parallelogram $ABCD$ with the three indicated corresponding angles equal to $70^\circ$.
answer.worked: Draw $DC$. Construct the two rays at $70^\circ$ to the rightward baseline. Choose $A$ on the ray from $D$, then construct the corresponding $70^\circ$ angle at $A$. The line through $A$ meets the ray from $C$ at $B$.

answer.short: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel: $AD\parallel BC$ and $AB\parallel DC$.
answer.worked: The equal corresponding $70^\circ$ angles at $D$ and $C$ give $AD\parallel BC$. The equal corresponding $70^\circ$ angles at $D$ and $A$ give $AB\parallel DC$. Thus both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Check that the opposite sides are equal in length.

answer.worked: Measure all four sides with a ruler. The measurements should give $AB=DC$ and $AD=BC$, allowing for construction and measurement accuracy. Numerical lengths depend on the chosen construction.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Draw the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$, and check that their intersection $M$ is the midpoint of each diagonal.

answer.short: $AM=MC$ and $BM=MD$, allowing for measurement accuracy; $M$ is the midpoint of both diagonals.
answer.worked: Draw $AC$ and $BD$ on the construction and label their intersection $M$. Measure the two portions of each diagonal. The measurements should give $AM=MC$ and $BM=MD$, allowing for construction and measurement accuracy. Hence $M$ is the midpoint of each diagonal.

spec.description: Representative construction completed with both diagonals and their intersection M; numerical lengths remain unspecified.
